absent: Locking and synchronization rules for pin control, platform devices, PNP and protection keys.
Internals of pinctrl_dev, pinctrl_map, pinmux_ops, pinconf_ops and device-tree parsing beyond the wrappers.
Platform bus, generic device and driver core behaviour, resource allocation and DMA mapping.
GPIO chip, device node, sequence file and firmware node semantics.
Real architecture protection-key allocation, access control and VMA handling.
Intel SCU IPC device command semantics and error codes.
Simple framebuffer and NAND driver behaviour beyond platform data layouts.
PNP device layout and real resource assignment.

findings.text: Generic pin configuration parameters occupy low numeric values with a terminator marking end of the generic range at 0x7F and an absolute ceiling at 0xFF, leaving higher values for custom use.

A combined pin configuration value stores its parameter selector in the low eight bits and its numeric argument in the next twenty-four bits, with helpers to extract either field and to rebuild a combined value from a parameter plus argument pair.

Pin configuration metadata uses two read-only descriptors: one pairs a parameter with human-readable display and format strings plus an argument flag and optional value table, the other maps a device-tree property name to a parameter with a default and allowed values.

Three convenience wrappers adapt device-tree configuration parsing for group scope, pin scope, or automatic inference by forwarding to a common mapper with the corresponding map kind, using an invalid kind to trigger inference.
Four standard pin control state keys exist for default, init, idle and sleep operation.

A pin group binds a name to an array of pin numbers with its length, while a pin descriptor binds a numeric identifier to an optional name and driver private pointer; helpers construct anonymous pins, named pins, and groups from name plus array and length.
A GPIO range links pin control and GPIO numbering through list linkage, name, identifiers, base offsets, pin count, optional pin index array, and owning chip pointer.
A pin controller driver implements counting of groups, lookup of group name and pins, debug display, and translation plus release of device-tree mappings.

A controller description aggregates name, pin table and count, operation vectors for grouping, multiplexing and configuration, owner reference, optional generic parameter tables, and a consumer-linkage flag.
Bit zero of pin function flags marks a function as GPIO capable.
A pin function pairs a name with a set of group names plus count and flags, with distinct constructors for plain functions and for GPIO-marked functions.
In the reviewed configuration the device-tree pin controller lookup always yields a null handle, indicating no lookup support.

Without architecture key support there is a single key with zero as default and sole allocated value, allocation always fails, freeing always reports invalid argument, access updates succeed trivially, execute-only and protection-override queries yield zero, flag mask is zero, and enablement reports false.
Broadcom NAND platform data carries a chip-select index, optional probe-type strings, and ECC step size plus strength.

Simple framebuffer platform data gives width, height, stride and format name, while each format entry gives bits per pixel, channel layouts for colour and transparency, and a four-character code; a canned table covers common sixteen, twenty-four and thirty-two bit RGB variants.

AMD FCH power management uses base 0xFED80300 with decode-enable at offset 0x00, SMBus select mask covering bits 20 through 19, scratch at 0x80 and S5 reset status at 0xC0; the x86 Apple machine predicate is constantly false in this configuration.
Intel SCU IPC platform data pairs a memory resource with an interrupt number.

Intel SCU IPC registration helpers capture caller module identity for managed and unmanaged cases, and the short command helper forwards to the sized variant reusing the input length for both length fields.

A platform device combines name, numeric identifier and auto-identifier flag, embedded generic device, DMA mask and parameters, resource array with count, identifier-table entry, MFD cell link and architecture data, with helpers to fetch the identifier entry, test bus membership, and convert from the embedded device.
Platform device identifiers reserve -1 for none and -2 for automatic allocation.

In the reviewed fallback configuration the managed helpers for fetching plus mapping a resource, mapping by index, or mapping by name all yield an error pointer encoding invalid argument rather than a usable mapping.
Platform creation parameters bundle parent, firmware and software nodes, node-reuse flag, name and identifier, resource vector, private data with length, DMA mask and property list.
Thin wrappers build creation parameters for resource-plus-data, resource-only with no parent or data, or data-only cases and delegate to a full registration routine.

A platform driver supplies probe, remove, shutdown, suspend and resume hooks with generic driver state, identifier table, deferred-probe control and a self-managed DMA flag that lets special drivers own their I/O address space, plus a helper converting from the embedded driver.

Driver registration, one-shot probing, module and built-in lifecycle, multi-driver registration and bundled creation helpers capture module and name identity and delegate to underscored core routines, with probe variants wiring init and exit handling.

Platform power hooks for suspend, resume, freeze, thaw, poweroff and restore are null in the reviewed build, with a sleep-operations helper expanding either to those null assignments or to nothing depending on variant, and the legacy SH early-device test always reports false.
Driver private data for a platform device lives in the embedded generic device and is accessed through thin get and set wrappers.
Pin control clients move among default, init, idle and sleep states across initial setup, active operation, idling and suspend.
Platform devices advance from registration through probe to active use, with optional suspend-resume and freeze-thaw-restore plus poweroff cycles, ending in remove or shutdown.

Plug-and-play helpers treat a null resource as invalid, absence of the disabled flag as enabled, and zero start with zero end as zero length, otherwise returning stored bounds, flags or length with type-specific defaults for missing port, memory, interrupt and DMA entries; the underlying lookup always yields null here.
Plug-and-play names are limited to 50 characters.

Because the reviewed PNP lookup always yields null, callers observe default flags and zero or negative-one placeholders rather than hardware resources, so validity checks must precede use of returned values.
